items.rationale: The power comes first: 3^2 = 9. Then multiplication: 2*9 = 18. Last comes addition: 10 + 18 = 28.
Excel applies the minus sign before the power, so it works out (-3)^2 = 9. To get -9, write =-(3^2), with brackets.
10% is just 0.1, and it is worked out before the addition, so the result is 100 + 0.1 = 100.1. To add 10% of 100, you would write =100*(1+10%), which is 110.

The brackets force 1+E2 first, so the cost is multiplied by (1 + duty). =C2*1+E2+D2/B2 adds the duty rate itself to the cost. The other two put the freight inside the duty calculation, which gives a wrong total.
